Commentary.Commentary: Right then, an ominous start to the tour and it is frustrating not just for the players but for the spectators inside the stadium as well who came in large numbers to watch this highly-anticipated clash and also for all cricket lovers around the world. No need to worry though as the tour is a long one and the 2nd T20I is coming up next. South Africa will take on India on 12th December, Tuesday at St George's Park in Gqeberha. That game will begin at 8.30 pm IST (3 pm GMT) but you can as always join us sooner for the build-up. Till then, take care and goodbye!

ALAS! THE MATCH HAS BEEN ABANDONED DUE TO RAIN! Unfortunately, the rain has had the final say in this series opener. Handshakes all around as persistent rain has forced the fixture to be called off without even the toss possible. A huge disappointment for the sell-out Durban crowd and even the players.

UPDATE - 9.13 pm IST (3.43 pm GMT) - It is still raining steadily and things do not look promising at the moment. Live visuals show the match officials hovering near the square with their umbrellas on. Even though it has been a drizzle since the start, the rain has to completely stop for the ground staff to start working on the outfield. Stick around and let's remain hopeful for some positive news.

UPDATE - 8.42 pm IST (3.12 pm GMT) - The rain continues to fall at Kingsmead! It is a steady drizzle at the moment and the rain gods seem to be in no mood to show mercy. It is extremely frustrating for everyone involved, especially for the sell-out Durban crowd. Fingers crossed for a positive update!

UPDATE - 8.10 pm (2.40 pm GMT) - The waiting game continues! Considering the amount of time lost so far, we might start losing overs soon, if not already. The live pictures show Indian players and support staff chit-chatting in their dressing room as they wait for the rain to stop. All we can do right now is wait and hope for the rain to subside. Stay tuned for more updates.

UPDATE - 7.36 pm IST (2.06 pm GMT) - Nothing much has changed since the last update as it continues to drizzle at Kingsmead. In case you were wondering, we will start losing overs from 8.10 pm IST (2.40 pm GMT). So we still have time on our hands to entertain the prospects of a full game. We will keep you posted.

UPDATE - 7.00 pm IST (1.30 pm GMT) - It is still raining and the covers are firmly in place. The toss has been delayed in this first T20I. Let's keep our fingers crossed that the weather clears up soon and we can have some action. As we wait for the rain to relent, you can switch tabs and follow the action from the third T20I between India Women and England Women. Or if you are craving some Men's T20I action, you can follow the series decider between Zimbabwe and Ireland. Stick around for more news.

UPDATE - 6.46 pm IST (1.16 pm GMT) - Uh oh! We are afraid that this piece of news is a bit of a mood spoiler, but it is currently drizzling at Kingsmead, and the covers are on. The positive news is that the radar looks fine and the rain is likely to stay away during match hours. Let's hope that we have the toss on time and get a prompt start to the game. Stay tuned for further updates.

On the other hand, India, led by Suryakumar Yadav, come into this series on the back of an impressive series win against Australia. The Men in Blue have shown confidence in youth but have also added depth to the side with the inclusion of Shubman Gill, Ravindra Jadeja, Kuldeep Yadav, and Mohammed Siraj. Other than the skipper, the onus will be on Yashasvi Jaiswal, Ruturaj Gaikwad, and Shreyas Iyer to continue playing the fearless brand of cricket, while Rinku Singh and Jitesh Sharma will be entrusted with the finisher role. Fresh off his final over heroics in the last outing against Australia, Arshdeep Singh will be high on confidence, while Mohammed Siraj and Ravi Bishnoi will also have a key role to play with the ball. Can India start their tour on a winning note? Or will it be the Aiden Markram-led unit who emerges victorious in Durban? Join us for the ride to find out. Toss and team news coming up in a bit.

South Africa are returning to action for the first time since that heartbreak in the ODI World Cup semi-final against Australia. In an effort to manage the workload ahead of the Test series, the Proteas have rested some of their all-format players and called up a few fresh faces for the T20I series. That said, they do have Reeza Hendricks, Aiden Markram, Heinrich Klaasen, and David Miller as the T20I regulars in the batting department. Keshav Maharaj and Tabraiz Shamsi form the crux of their spin department, but it is their pace attack that will be tested, and Marco Jansen and Gerald Coetzee will have to shoulder the responsibility.

The stage is set for the start of South Africa's action-packed summer of men's international cricket through a three-match T20I series against the number one-ranked T20I side, India. Hello and a warm welcome, folks, to our coverage of the first T20I between South Africa and India at Kingsmead in Durban. A riveting prospect awaits us as two white-ball powerhouses go head-to-head in the shortest format of the game.

With the wounds of the ODI World Cup final heartbreak still fresh despite the recent series win against Australia, India have embarked on their tour to South Africa, a land where they have yet to secure a Test series victory. The bigger narrative will unfold later in the Test series, but before that, the white-ball series will take centre stage. The tour kicks off with a three-match T20I series, with the opening game to be played at Kingsmead in Durban. With not many T20Is left before the T20 World Cup, this series bears significant importance for both sides as part of their build-up for the event. South Africa's previous T20I assignment was before the ODI World Cup against Australia, where they suffered a 3-0 hammering against Australia at home. The Proteas think tank have rested some of their senior players in a bid to prepare them for the Test series to follow. Aiden Markram will lead the side possessing a good blend of youth and experience. The hosts were dealt a blow in their preparations for this series with Lungi Ngidii ruled out of the series due to an ankle sprain. Beuran Hendricks has been named as his replacement while Marco Jansen and Gerald Coetzee are the two usual suspects in the pace department. The uncapped duo of Ottniel Baartman and Nandre Burger are the other seam bowling options Aiden Markramd will have at his disposal. Fresh from their ODI World Cup exploits, Keshav Maharaj and Tabraiz Shamsi continue to shoulder the responsibility in the spin department. There will be no shortage of firepower for the hosts with the presence of Reeza Hendricks, Heinrich Klaasen, Aiden Markram, and David Miller in their ranks. On the other hand, India will continue to field their young brigade, which is coming off a successful T20I series against Australia. The Suryakumar Yadav-led unit now face their biggest test yet against a competitive South African team who are a force to reckon with in their backyard. The addition of Shubman Gill strengthens their batting even more, which already has the likes of Yashasvi Jaiswal, Shreyas Iyer, and Suryakumar Yadav. Rinku Singh and Jitesh Sharma have emerged as strong contenders for the finisher role, and it will be interesting to see if they live up to the expectations. Ravindra Jadeja and Kuldeep Yadav return to the side, as does Mohammed Siraj, which adds depth to the Indian bowling attack. Leggie Ravi Bishnoi has been rewarded for his heroics as he became the top-ranked T20I bowler and he will be eager to continue his form. Arshdeep Singh, Mukesh Kumar, and Deepak Chahar leaked a lot of runs across the five games against Australia, but they have another opportunity to make a strong case for a spot in the T20 World Cup squad. The last time these two sides faced off in a bilateral T20I series in the Rainbow Nation, India clinched the series with a 2-1 scoreline. Will the Men in Blue rise to the challenge? Or will South Africa draw the first blood? We will find out soon enough.
